name: age-filter
description:
Exercises the max_age_days branch, which the main import scenario deliberately disables by passing 0. Any non-zero age limit makes the importer call parse_time(scan_end) on whatever gvmd put in last_report, and parse_time defaults to RFC3339 and RAISES on anything it cannot read -- a Starlark builtin returning an error aborts the entire run, so the script's `if ended != None` guard can never fire. That makes the exact timestamp gvmd emits load-bearing.

Both forms a live gvmd 25.2.1 was observed to produce are RFC3339 and parse cleanly: '2026-08-16T13:57:09Z' from get_tasks, and '2026-08-16T08:57:09-05:00' from get_reports when a timezone= filter term is supplied (note the colon in the offset -- gvmd does not emit the bare -0500 form here, even though the %FT%T%z format string is present in the binary). get_tasks ignores timezone= entirely and always answers in UTC, and last_report/report/scan_end is the only timestamp this importer reads, so the Z form below is the realistic case. A 10-year window keeps the assertion stable rather than expiring as the recording ages.
